cards.headline: Microsoft and OpenAI End Exclusive Deal
cards.blurb: Microsoft and OpenAI have ended their exclusive and revenue-sharing deal, marking a significant shift in their partnership. This change allows OpenAI to explore other collaborations and revenue streams. The exact terms of the new agreement are not publicly disclosed.
cards.why_it_matters: This change could impact the development of AI models and services, as OpenAI may now be able to partner with other companies, potentially leading to increased innovation and competition in the AI space. This, in turn, could affect the cost and accessibility of AI-powered tools for businesses and consumers.

sources.title: Microsoft and OpenAI end their exclusive and revenue-sharing deal

cards.headline: 40k AI Contractors' Voice Samples Stolen
cards.blurb: A massive data breach at Mercor has resulted in the theft of 4TB of voice samples from 40,000 AI contractors. This sensitive data could be used for malicious purposes, such as creating deepfakes or training AI models for phishing attacks. The breach highlights the importance of data security in the AI development process.
cards.why_it_matters: The stolen voice samples could be used to compromise the security of voice-activated systems, such as virtual assistants or voice-based authentication systems, potentially leading to significant financial and reputational losses for affected companies. This incident also underscores the need for robust data protection measures in the AI industry.

sources.title: 4TB of voice samples just stolen from 40k AI contractors at Mercor

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot Moves to Usage-Based Billing
cards.blurb: GitHub Copilot is transitioning to a usage-based billing model, which will charge users based on their actual usage of the service. This change is intended to provide more flexibility and cost predictability for developers. The new billing model will be based on the number of lines of code generated by Copilot.
cards.why_it_matters: This change could make GitHub Copilot more attractive to developers who only occasionally use the service, as they will only pay for what they use. This, in turn, could lead to increased adoption of AI-powered development tools and more efficient coding practices, ultimately driving innovation in the software development industry.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot is moving to usage-based billing

cards.headline: AI Code Agents to Reshape Developer Landscape
cards.blurb: The emergence of AI code agents is expected to bring significant changes to the developer landscape in 2026. These agents will be able to automate routine coding tasks, freeing up developers to focus on more complex and creative work. According to industry experts, AI code agents will revolutionize the way developers work and collaborate.
cards.why_it_matters: The adoption of AI code agents could lead to increased productivity and efficiency in software development, as well as improved code quality and reduced errors. This, in turn, could have a significant impact on the tech industry as a whole, enabling companies to bring products to market faster and more reliably, and driving innovation in areas like AI, cloud computing, and cybersecurity.

sources.title: AI Code Agents 2026: Big Changes Reshaping Developers

cards.headline: New Intel Driver Enables Dedicated System Memory for iGPU
cards.blurb: Intel has released a new driver that allows users to dedicate up to 93% of system memory to the integrated GPU (iGPU), enabling support for larger AI models and more demanding workloads. This feature is particularly useful for applications that require significant VRAM, such as AI training and graphics rendering.
cards.why_it_matters: This development could have significant implications for the field of AI research and development, as it enables researchers to train larger and more complex models on consumer-grade hardware. This, in turn, could lead to breakthroughs in areas like computer vision, natural language processing, and autonomous vehicles, and drive innovation in the tech industry as a whole.

sources.title: New Intel driver lets you dedicate 93% of system memory to the iGPU for VRAM, enabling support for larger AI models

cards.headline: Dutch Central Bank Ditches AWS for Lidl's European Cloud
cards.blurb: The Dutch central bank has announced that it will be switching from Amazon Web Services (AWS) to Lidl's European Cloud for its cloud computing needs. This move is seen as a significant win for Lidl, which is expanding its cloud offerings to compete with major players like AWS and Microsoft Azure.
cards.why_it_matters: This decision reflects a growing trend of organizations seeking alternative cloud providers to avoid vendor lock-in and reduce costs. The move could also have implications for the broader cloud computing market, as companies like Lidl and other regional players challenge the dominance of major cloud providers like AWS and Microsoft.

sources.title: Dutch central bank ditches AWS and chooses Lidl for European Cloud

cards.headline: Geely Unveils China's First Purpose-Built Robotaxi
cards.blurb: Geely has announced the launch of China's first purpose-built robotaxi, which is designed specifically for autonomous ride-hailing services. The vehicle features a range of advanced sensors and AI-powered systems, including lidar, cameras, and radar.
cards.why_it_matters: The development of purpose-built robotaxis like Geely's could accelerate the adoption of autonomous vehicles in the ride-hailing industry, reducing labor costs and improving safety. This, in turn, could have significant implications for the future of transportation, urban planning, and the environment, as autonomous vehicles become increasingly integrated into our daily lives.

sources.title: Geely Says This Is China’s First Purpose-Built Robotaxi. I'm Not So Sure

cards.headline: Dense Retrievers Align with LLM Utility via Distillation
cards.blurb: Researchers have proposed a new method for aligning dense retrievers with large language models (LLMs) using distillation. This approach enables the development of more efficient and effective information retrieval systems, which can be used in a range of applications, including search engines and question-answering systems.
cards.why_it_matters: The alignment of dense retrievers with LLMs could lead to significant improvements in the performance and efficiency of natural language processing systems, enabling more accurate and relevant search results, and driving innovation in areas like AI-powered customer service and content recommendation.

cards.headline: Asahi Linux Progress with Linux 7.0
cards.blurb: The Asahi Linux project has made significant progress with the release of Linux 7.0, which includes a range of improvements and enhancements for Apple Silicon-based systems. The new release provides better support for Apple's M1 and M2 chips, as well as improved performance and power management.
cards.why_it_matters: The development of Asahi Linux could enable more widespread adoption of Linux on Apple devices, providing users with a more open and customizable alternative to macOS. This, in turn, could drive innovation in the Linux community and enable new use cases for Apple hardware, such as running Linux-based servers or developing Linux-based applications.

cards.headline: The Internet of Things Continues to Evolve
cards.blurb: The Internet of Things (IoT) is continuing to evolve, with new technologies and applications emerging all the time. From smart homes and cities to industrial automation and healthcare, the IoT is transforming the way we live and work. According to industry experts, the IoT will have a significant impact on various sectors, including manufacturing, transportation, and energy.
cards.why_it_matters: The IoT has the potential to drive significant economic and social benefits, from improved efficiency and productivity to enhanced safety and convenience. However, it also raises important questions about data privacy, security, and governance, which must be addressed in order to realize the full potential of the IoT and ensure that its benefits are equitably distributed.

sources.title: The incredible Internet of Things - The Tribune
